title: Final: ClashService
sub: Find the bugs in the full listing
cards/0/task: This is the whole ClashService sent for review. Mark as many bugs as you can: equality and dictionary, async, threads, collections, recursion, exceptions, Unity null. You need at least 18.
cards/0/bugs/0/why: Equal keys land in different dictionary drawers, so the cache cannot find its own keys and keeps growing, and every call recomputes everything.
cards/0/bugs/1/why: Once GetHashCode is fixed and depends on the fields, changing a field after insertion "loses" the entry: it can be neither found nor removed.
cards/0/bugs/2/title: Id ignores ModelId (and Key may be null)
cards/0/bugs/2/why: Elements from different models with the same number are indistinguishable: buckets and comparisons mix them up. A missing Key gives a NullReferenceException.
cards/0/bugs/3/why: The caller cannot wait for completion or catch the error. If a task throws, Completed never fires; in Unity the exception only shows up in the console, in .NET without a synchronization context the process crashes.
cards/0/bugs/4/title: Closure over the loop variable i
cards/0/bugs/4/why: Tasks usually see i == 8, the filter selects nothing, and the service finds zero clashes. The main bug of the listing.
cards/0/bugs/5/title: Splitting by Id % 8 breaks the pairs
cards/0/bugs/5/why: Elements from different buckets are never compared, so some clashes can never be found. Negative Ids give a negative remainder.
cards/0/bugs/6/why: The inner loop re-runs the filter for every outer element: n² predicate calls and repeated computation of the source.
cards/0/bugs/7/why: List<T> is not thread-safe: writing from eight threads loses items and throws exceptions.
cards/0/bugs/8/title: Non-atomic counter with a misleading name
cards/0/bugs/8/why: _processed++ from several threads loses increments (Interlocked is needed), and the name promises "processed" while it counts clashes.
cards/0/bugs/9/title: a.Id < b.Id drops pairs with equal Ids
cards/0/bugs/9/why: Elements from different models with the same ElementId are never compared, so a clash between them is never found.
cards/0/bugs/10/why: The list changes during enumeration: InvalidOperationException on the next step. Plus quadratic work. Use RemoveAll.
cards/0/bugs/11/why: ContainsKey, then the indexer: two lookups instead of one. Fixed with TryGetValue.
cards/0/bugs/12/title: Cache is never reset and exposes its internal list
cards/0/bugs/12/why: After removal, import and new clashes the cache holds stale queries, and a mutable internal list is handed out.
cards/0/bugs/13/title: Recursion with no guard against rings or depth
cards/0/bugs/13/why: A ring in Parent/Children or a very deep tree causes StackOverflowException. In .NET it cannot be caught and the process ends; in an IL2CPP build the app crashes.
cards/0/bugs/14/why: Heights are inexact in the last digits, so an element on the level is not recognized as such. A tolerance is needed.
cards/0/bugs/15/why: Only Import remains in the trace, and the real place of failure vanishes. You need throw;.
cards/0/bugs/16/why: The same error gets logged at every level, and the log fills up with duplicates. And LogError(ex.Message) drops the stack trace: use Debug.LogException(ex) where the error is handled.
cards/0/bugs/17/why: It catches everything, even what cannot be fixed here. Use specific types (IOException, JsonException).
cards/0/bugs/18/why: For an empty file or the content "null", AddRange(null) throws ArgumentNullException. The cache is not reset after the import, and every clash from the JSON gets its own copies of Element, unrelated to the model's elements.
cards/0/bugs/19/why: File.ReadAllText blocks the thread. On Unity's main thread the game freezes while the file is read.
cards/0/bugs/20/why: For a destroyed GameObject (fake null), ?. does not work as a check and gives MissingReferenceException.
cards/0/bugs/21/why: The class is not a MonoBehaviour, so the Inspector will not fill the field. It is always null, and Highlight silently does nothing.
cards/0/bugs/22/why: The link can be broken from either side, even into a ring. And two-way references are a loop for serialization: Newtonsoft throws "Self referencing loop detected".
cards/1/q: Which bug is the main one, the reason the service "silently finds zero clashes"?
cards/1/options/0: Closure over the loop variable i in Task.Run
cards/1/explain: All tasks see i == 8, and the filter Id % 8 == 8 lets no element through. The other bugs break the result less often or loudly, while this one empties it without a single error.
cards/1/wrong/1: async void hides exceptions, but it does not blank the result.
cards/1/wrong/2: float == breaks the level check, not the clash search.
cards/2/q: Which bugs in the listing show up "intermittently", not on every run? Pick all that apply.
cards/2/options/2: Closure over i (depends on when the tasks start)
cards/2/explain: Races and the closure depend on timing. Remove inside foreach fails every time there is something to remove: that error is deterministic.
cards/3/q: Which of these errors in the listing cannot be caught with try/catch?
cards/3/explain: In .NET a stack overflow ends the process immediately, and no catch runs. The other three are ordinary exceptions and can be caught. So the guard against rings must be in the code up front.
cards/4/q: Put the steps of a Dictionary key lookup in order.
cards/4/items/1: Pick a drawer (bucket) by the hash
cards/4/items/2: Walk the entries of that drawer
cards/4/items/3: For entries with the same hash, compare keys with Equals
cards/4/explain: If equal keys have different GetHashCode values, step 2 leads to another drawer, and even if the drawer matches, the stored hash does not. Equals is never reached.
cards/5/q: Fix the launcher: the right return type and a list materialized once.
cards/5/explain: Instead of async void you need async Task, so callers can await and catch errors. ToList() pins the data once, and tasks do not recompute a lazy query. Where materializes nothing by itself.
cards/6/q: Which line erases the real call stack of the exception?
cards/6/explain: The throw ex; line restarts the trace at the current place. The correct form is throw;. The logging above does not erase the stack, but it makes the error "noisy".
cards/7/q: Match each bug with its symptom.
cards/7/pairs/0/1: The cache cannot find its own keys
cards/7/pairs/4/1: The process dies, catch does not help
cards/8/q: What is the best way to redo ElementKey?
cards/8/options/0: An immutable struct: readonly struct with IEquatable, GetHashCode and == (or a readonly record struct)
cards/8/options/1: Keep the class and write GetHashCode over the mutable fields
cards/8/options/2: Use a string of ModelId + ElementId concatenated on every call
cards/8/explain: A key must be immutable, with Equals and GetHashCode consistent; a struct with IEquatable<T> creates no garbage and is not boxed. In .NET with C# 10, a readonly record struct generates all of this, while in Unity (C# 9) you write such a struct by hand.
cards/8/wrong/1: A hash over mutable fields loses entries after an edit.
cards/8/wrong/2: Concatenating a string on every call creates garbage, and the key stays flimsy.
